messages.subject: Issue understanding "groupComparisonTMT"
parts:
Dear Author,

I am reaching out to discuss my difficulty understanding the results obtained from the msstatsTMT package. Specifically, we ran the groupComparisonTMT function using the compare_analysis = groupComparisonTMT(data = processed_data, contrast.matrix = comparison, moderated = TRUE) command and exported the results to a CSV file using write.csv(compare_analysis$ComparisonResult, "comparison1.csv").

Upon reviewing the output file, we observed two issues. Firstly, when we examined the top proteins in the "processed_data$ProteinLevelData" data, we found that the direction of log2FC values was inconsistent for multiple proteins. Additionally, we attempted to calculate the t-test and log2FC values manually, but the results were not consistent with those generated by msstatsTMT. We would appreciate any insights into how the log2FC values are calculated and how we can better understand the results.

As a potential solution, we attempted to calculate the log2FC values using the following Python code, adjusting for the number of samples based on the plexing used:

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

def log2_fold_change(x, y):
    return np.log2((np.mean(x) + 1e-8) / (np.mean(y) + 1e-8)) ##added a small value 1e-8 so that if denominator is zero we still have some value that will allow to run the function normally

data = pd.read_csv("btvssst_processprotein.csv", skipinitialspace=True)

data['Abundance'] = data['Abundance'].astype(float)

results = pd.DataFrame(columns=["Protein", "Label", "log2FC", "t-statistic", "p-value", "adj.p-value"]) ##output we needed in the csv file

total_samples_BT = 13
total_samples_SST = 16

for protein in data["Protein"].unique():
    protein_data = data[data["Protein"] == protein]

    bt_values = protein_data[protein_data["Condition"] == "BT"]["Abundance"]
    sst_values = protein_data[protein_data["Condition"] == "SST"]["Abundance"]

    if len(bt_values) == 0 or len(sst_values) == 0:  # ADDED condition to remove any protein present if only in one condition
        continue

    bt_values = np.append(BT_values, [0] * (total_samples_BT - len(ssm_values)))
    sst_values = np.append(sst_values, [0] * (total_samples_SST - lenbt_values)))

    t_statistic, p_value = ttest_ind(bt_values, sst_values, equal_var=False)
    log2fc = log2_fold_change(bt_values, sst_values)

    results = results.append({
        "Protein": protein,
        "Label": "BTvsSST",
        "log2FC": log2fc,
        "t-statistic": t_statistic,  # Added t-statistic to the results DataFrame
        "p-value": p_value,
        "adj.p-value": None
    }, ignore_index=True)

results["adj.p-value"] = results["p-value"] * len(results) / (np.arange(len(results)) + 1)

results.to_csv("t_test_results_bt-sst.csv", index=False)

However, even with this approach, we still observed inconsistencies with the results generated by msstatsTMT.

We would greatly appreciate any assistance you can provide in better understanding these results and determining potential solutions to these issues.

Thank you for your time and attention.

Best regards,

Devender

parts:
Hi,


do you have a specific example eaxmple of protein-level data to compare the results?
Would https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.jproteome.2c00834 and https://docs.lib.purdue.edu/open_access_dissertations/636/ help as a reference?
In short: we fit a linear model to protein-level data (summarization output from the dataProcess function) and log-fold change is calculated based on estimated parameters of this model and selected contrats. Typically, it will be a difference between estimated Condition effects.

Kind regards,
Mateusz
